reader: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code session acting as the step-04 LLM by hand, 2026-10-31); source images 04-diagramok/renders/page-{4,7,8,9,10}.png (250 dpi); no PDF vector paths or PDF text used
method: Image analysis of the 250 dpi renders (allowed by the prompt): the grey plot rectangle and its white gridlines were located by pixel colour; the px->value maps were fitted on the gridlines with the printed tick values (max residual 0.13 axis units on x, 1.6 psi on 800-psig y scales); each curve was followed by its legend colour column by column (nearest colour cluster to the previous position) from its zero-flow start; points sampled at every labelled x gridline and every 1/20 of the x span, plus start and end. Every extracted point was overlaid on the render and checked by eye; two grey curves on the 2C/4C air chart that end where they meet the 4C 1 psi curve were cut at that junction by hand. Page 4 band read from the two boundary-line pixel positions at 7 columns and fitted as straight lines.

charts.title: Cracking and Reseal Pressures at 70°F (20°C), CA and CPA Series
charts.note: The chart is a shaded band between two straight lines (reseal pressure range for a given cracking pressure); both boundaries read at every 50 psi gridline. Values below 0 psi reseal are marked 'Back Pressure'. The dashed example (cracking 450 psi -> reseal 390 to 450 psi) agrees with the read lines (lower 394, upper 448). Top axis (bar) and right axis (bar) restate the primary scales. Left axis runs from -50 to 600 psi.

charts.title: Flow Data at 70°F (20°C), C Series, Air, 2C, 4C Series
charts.note: Secondary scales (top: L/min, right: bar) only restate the primary axes; values read on the primary bottom/left axes. Series = nominal cracking pressure per the page legend. 2C 10 psi curve merges into the 2C 1 psi curve at about 2.5 std ft3/min; 4C 10 psi ends where it meets the 4C 1 psi curve (about 6.5 std ft3/min, 14 psig) and 4C 25 psi where it meets it at about 11 std ft3/min, 36 psig. The 2C curves leave the plot at the 100 psig top edge.
